about.title: About
about.description: I help organizations make their digital products, processes, and culture more accessible and usable.
about.lead: Digital accessibility engineer focused on inclusive architecture.
about.journeyP1: My journey in the digital ecosystem began in 2006, not behind an IDE, but in customer service. This foundational experience taught me that behind every line of code, there is a real human need.
about.journeyP2: When transitioning to software engineering, I carried this obsession with user experience with me. I quickly realized that the "standard" web excluded millions. Since then, I've specialized in transforming complex interfaces into inclusive and technically flawless experiences.
values: Inclusion: Designing for the edge ensures quality for the center.
Education: Knowledge is only valuable when shared.
Quality: Accessibility is synonymous with clean code.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.description: Commitment to digital inclusion and compliance with web accessibility guidelines.

sections.heading: Commitment
sections.text: Bruno Pulis is committed to ensuring this website is accessible to all people, regardless of their physical, sensory, or cognitive abilities. We believe digital accessibility is a fundamental right and an essential pillar of web quality.

sections.heading: Standards Adopted
sections.text: This website follows the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, Level AA, from the W3C. This includes, among other practices:
items: Semantic HTML with proper landmarks and heading hierarchy;
Sufficient color contrast between text and background;
Visible and predictable keyboard navigation;
Alternative text for informative images;
Support for screen readers and assistive technologies;
Text resizing without loss of functionality.

sections.heading: Testing and Tools
sections.text: We conduct periodic accessibility testing using:
items: WAVE (WebAIM);
Axe DevTools;
Lighthouse (Chrome DevTools);
Screen readers (NVDA, VoiceOver);
Exclusive keyboard navigation.

sections.heading: Compatibility
sections.text: The site is compatible with modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) and common assistive technologies. For the best experience, we recommend keeping your browser and screen reader up to date.

sections.heading: Report Barriers
sections.text: If you encounter any accessibility barriers while browsing this site, please let us know. Your contribution is essential for continuous improvement.
sections.contact: Send a message through the contact form or directly to brunopulis@protonmail.com.

accessibleSites.title: Accessible Site Development
accessibleSites.description: Websites that truly work for everyone.
accessibleSites.lead: Accessible websites are interfaces that follow international development standards, aiming for the best understanding by all people.
accessibleSites.sectionTitle: What it means to build a truly accessible website
paragraphs: It's not installing a plugin. It's not adding an accessible mode button. It's not passing an automated validator and celebrating zero errors.

Real accessibility starts in information architecture and runs through every markup decision, from <abbr title="Cascade Style Sheets">CSS</abbr> and JavaScript to deployment. It's a development posture, not a feature.
When I join a project, accessibility isn't the last step. It's the criterion that guides everything else.

howIWork.intro: Every project starts with understanding: the product, the audience, the flows that need to work. From there, technical decisions have context.
items: Definition of what needs to be done;
Markup of headings, lists, and tables;
Alternative text for images and graphics;
Language configuration and document metadata;
Accessible form fields (when applicable);
Verification with tools like PAC 2024 and Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker
howIWork.deadline: Delivery time: 5 business days after signing the service contract.

techs.intro: I primarily work with tools I know well that produce clean code by default:
items: WordPress: theme development and customizations focused on semantics and standards;
Astro: for static or hybrid content sites, focusing on performance and correct markup;
Eleventy (11ty): for editorial projects, blogs, and sites that prioritize simple, well-structured HTML;
HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: without framework dependencies when the project doesn't require them.
techs.footer: I don't sell a stack. I choose what makes sense for the problem.

notDo.text: I don't deliver sites with accessibility overlays — those widgets that promise to "make any site accessible" with a script.
notDo.text2: They don't work, they create conflicts with assistive technologies, and they generate a false sense of compliance.

audience.text: This service is for those building something new or redoing something that doesn't work well — and wants the result to be durable.
audience.text2: It could be a landing page, an institutional site, a portal with dynamic content, or a system with complex flows. What matters is that accessibility enters the project from the start, not as an afterthought.

start.quote: How to start? Tell me what you're building, what the context is, and what isn't working. From there, we talk.

audit.title: Accessibility Audit
audit.lead: My audits evaluate the accessibility of your website or application and provide practical recommendations for improvements.
audit.text1: They evaluate compliance with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at levels A and AA, following Brazilian Government accessibility and usability standards and ABNT standards: NBR 17060 and NBR 17225.
audit.text2: I don't provide complex reports — my reports are objective so you can fix issues practically. Analyzing the priority, impact, and legal risk of each issue found.
audit.text3: The report is delivered in spreadsheet format for easy integration into your development environment.

basic.text: The Basic Audit is a quick, honest read of your product. It's not a full audit. It's the first step: understanding the terrain before planning any move.
basic.recommended: Recommended for: small businesses, blogs, portfolios, sales pages.
includes: Prioritized list of issues: what blocks, what degrades, what's cosmetic;
Reference guidelines for each fix (WCAG, WAI-ARIA);
Accessible report ready to share with the team.
basic.deadline: Delivery time: 5 business days after signing the service contract.

complete.text: The Complete Audit is an in-depth analysis of your entire digital product. It includes all flows, components, and pages.
complete.recommended: Recommended for: medium to large companies, e-commerce, SaaS platforms.

audit.observation: Note: All audits include a 1-hour post-audit meeting to discuss the report, plus email support for any questions.

remediation.title: Document Remediation
remediation.description: Make your documents accessible to everyone.
remediation.lead: Document remediation aims to optimize and ensure that all people can access content broadly and unrestrictedly.
remediation.problemTitle: The problem is more common than it seems
remediation.problemText1: Most digital documents are born inaccessible. A PDF exported from Word, a data spreadsheet, a slide presentation — they may all look functional on screen, but for screen reader users, they're just noise or silence.
remediation.problemText2: This isn't carelessness. It's a lack of knowledge about how to structure documents so assistive technologies can interpret them correctly.

whatIDo.text: I take the document you already have and deliver an accessible version — with correct semantic structure, proper markup, and compliance with required technical standards.
includes: Markup of headings, lists, and tables;
Alternative text for images and graphics;
Verification with tools like PAC 2024 and Adobe Acrobat Accessibility Checker
whatIDo.deadline: Delivery time: 5 business days after signing the service contract.

docTypes.intro: I work with the most common formats in organizations' daily routine:
items: <abbr title="Portable Document File">PDF:</abbr> the most requested and the most complex to get right;
Word (.docx): remediation at the source, before generating the PDF;
PowerPoint (.pptx): slides with reading order and alternative text;
Excel (.xlsx): data tables with proper semantic markup.

when.summary: When does it make sense to hire this service?
when.text: If your organization needs to publish accessible documents — due to legal obligation, contract, or conviction — and the internal workflow doesn't consistently produce them yet, remediation is the most direct path.
when.text2: It also makes sense when there's a backlog of already published documents that need to be corrected.

remediation.observation: Note: the delivery time for remediations may vary depending on the content size.
